explanation: In China, hugging is not a common greeting and is generally reserved for close friends or family; sources note that touching strangers is disliked and that hugging someone you are not close to can overwhelm them. A handshake is the standard greeting, though young people may hug each other in Western style. At a social gathering, hugging a new acquaintance would likely feel intrusive.
local_tip: At a social gathering, offer a handshake or a slight nod instead of a hug, and only hug if a close Chinese friend initiates it.
regional_note: Sources note a generational split: younger Chinese may say "Hi" or hug each other as in the West, while older generations generally avoid body contact.

also_check.note: Bowing is the norm; hugging strangers is uncommon and can feel awkward.
Hugging friends and even new acquaintances is common and often welcomed.
La bise (cheek kisses) is standard among acquaintances; full hugs are more reserved for close friends.

sources.title: Chinese Etiquette Rules: The Do’s and Don’ts
